DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL: http://localhost:3001
          REDIS_HOST: localhost
          REDIS_PORT: 6379
          TEST_LOGIN_SECRET: e2e-test-secret-ci-only
          IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      # --- Desktop launch + test execution ---

      - name: Start frontend dev server
        if: runner.os != 'Windows'
        run: |
          cd apps/desktop
          pnpm vite preview --port 1420 &
          # Wait for dev server
          for i in $(seq 1 15); do
            if curl -sf http://localhost:1420 > /dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "Frontend dev server ready on :1420"
              break
            fi
            sleep 1
          done
        env:
          VITE_API_URL: http://localhost:3000
          VITE_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET: e2e-test-secret-ci-only

      - name: Run desktop E2E tests (macOS)
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          export CIPHERBOX_API_URL=http://localhost:3000
          export VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:3000
          export VITE_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET=e2e-test-secret-ci-only
          export RUST_LOG=info
          BINARY=target/debug/${{ matrix.binary-name }}
          chmod +x "$BINARY"
          DEV_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
          "$BINARY" --dev-key $DEV_KEY > /tmp/cipherbox-desktop.log 2>&1 &
          DESKTOP_PID=$!
          set +e
          bash tests/desktop-e2e/scripts/run-all.sh
          TEST_EXIT=$?
          set -e
          if [ "$TEST_EXIT" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "=== Desktop binary log ==="
            cat /tmp/cipherbox-desktop.log 2>/dev/null || echo "(no log file)"
          fi
          kill $DESKTOP_PID 2>/dev/null || true
          diskutil unmount force $HOME/CipherBox 2>/dev/null || true
          exit $TEST_EXIT

      - name: Run desktop E2E tests (Linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        env:
          CIPHERBOX_API_URL: http://localhost:3000
          VITE_API_URL: http://localhost:3000
          VITE_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET: e2e-test-secret-ci-only
          RUST_LOG: info
          DISPLAY: ':99'
          WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER: '1'
        run: |
          Xvfb :99 -screen 0 1024x768x24 &
          sleep 1
          BINARY=target/debug/${{ matrix.binary-name }}
          chmod +x "$BINARY"
          DEV_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
          "$BINARY" --dev-key $DEV_KEY > /tmp/cipherbox-desktop.log 2>&1 &
          DESKTOP_PID=$!
          set +e
          bash tests/desktop-e2e/scripts/run-all.sh
          TEST_EXIT=$?
          set -e
          if [ "$TEST_EXIT" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "=== Desktop binary log ==="
            cat /tmp/cipherbox-desktop.log 2>/dev/null || echo "(no log file)"
          fi
          kill $DESKTOP_PID 2>/dev/null || true
          fusermount3 -u $HOME/CipherBox 2>/dev/null || true
          exit $TEST_EXIT

      - name: Start frontend dev server (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          cd apps/desktop
          npx vite preview --port 1420 &
          for i in $(seq 1 15); do
            if curl -sf http://localhost:1420 > /dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "Frontend dev server ready on :1420"
              break
            fi
            sleep 1
          done
        env:
          VITE_API_URL: http://localhost:3000
          VITE_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET: e2e-test-secret-ci-only

      - name: Run desktop E2E tests (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          BINARY="target/debug/${{ matrix.binary-name }}"
          DEV_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
          LOGFILE="$RUNNER_TEMP/cipherbox-desktop.log"
          export DESKTOP_LOG="$LOGFILE"
          "$BINARY" --dev-key "$DEV_KEY" > "$LOGFILE" 2>&1 &
          DESKTOP_PID=$!
          set +e
          powershell -File "$PWD/tests/desktop-e2e/scripts/run-all.ps1"
          TEST_EXIT=$?
          set -e
          echo "=== Desktop binary log ==="
          cat "$LOGFILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "(no log file)"
          kill $DESKTOP_PID 2>/dev/null || true
          exit $TEST_EXIT
        env:
          CIPHERBOX_API_URL: http://localhost:3000
          VITE_API_URL: http://localhost:3000
          VITE_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET: e2e-test-secret-ci-only
          RUST_LOG: info

      # --- Failure artifacts ---

      - name: Collect logs on failure
        if: failure()
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p failure-logs
          cp /tmp/cipherbox-desktop.log failure-logs/ 2>/dev/null || true
          cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/cipherbox-desktop.log" failure-logs/ 2>/dev/null || true
          cp ~/Library/Logs/fuse-t/fuse-t.log failure-logs/ 2>/dev/null || true
          cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/api.log" failure-logs/ 2>/dev/null || true

      - name: Upload logs on failure
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: desktop-e2e-logs-${{ matrix.platform }}
          path: failure-logs/
          retention-days: 7

content.text:
**Found the smoking gun.** `rotation_deps.rs:53-58`: the read-key rotation **republishes rotated nodes with `write_sealed: None`** — write-plane preservation during a read-key rotation is explicitly *deferred to a Phase-72 follow-up*. So once a node is rotated, its published record has no write body. A subsequent owned-walk (`list_folder_owned`) requires the write body and **fails closed** → EIO → surfaced as EACCES over FUSE-T/SMB.

That's a real correctness gap, not infra. But I must confirm *why it's macOS-only* and reproduce it. Let me read the test harness setup and the run-all script to reproduce.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# run-all.sh -- Orchestrate the full desktop E2E test suite.
#
# Runs wait-for-mount, FUSE file I/O tests, and API round-trip tests.
# Reports an aggregate pass/fail summary and exits with the total failure count.
#
# Environment:
#   MOUNT_POINT   Path to FUSE mount (default: $HOME/CipherBox)
#   API_URL       Backend API URL (default: http://localhost:3000)
#   TEST_SECRET   test-login shared secret (default: e2e-test-secret-ci-only)

MOUNT_POINT="${MOUNT_POINT:-$HOME/CipherBox}"
API_URL="${API_URL:-http://localhost:3000}"
TEST_SECRET="${TEST_SECRET:-e2e-test-secret-ci-only}"

TOTAL_PASS=0
TOTAL_FAIL=0

echo "============================================"
echo "  CipherBox Desktop E2E Test Suite"
echo "============================================"
echo ""
echo "Mount point: $MOUNT_POINT"
echo "API URL:     $API_URL"
echo ""

# ---- Step 1: Wait for mount ----
echo "--- Step 1: Wait for mount ---"
if bash "$SCRIPT_DIR/wait-for-mount.sh" "$MOUNT_POINT"; then
  TOTAL_PASS=$((TOTAL_PASS + 1))
else
  echo "FATAL: Mount not available. Cannot continue."
  exit 1
fi
echo ""

set -e

if [ "$FUSE_FAILURES" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "FUSE operations: ALL PASSED"
else
  echo "FUSE operations: $FUSE_FAILURES FAILURE(S)"
  TOTAL_FAIL=$((TOTAL_FAIL + FUSE_FAILURES))
fi
echo ""

# ---- Step 3: API round-trip ----

set +e
TEST_SECRET="$TEST_SECRET" bash "$SCRIPT_DIR/test-round-trip.sh" "$MOUNT_POINT" "$API_URL"

set -e

if [ "$RT_FAILURES" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "API round-trip: ALL PASSED"

  TOTAL_FAIL=$((TOTAL_FAIL + RT_FAILURES))
fi
echo ""

set -e

if [ "$CONFLICT_FAILURES" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "Conflict detection: ALL PASSED"
else
  echo "Conflict detection: $CONFLICT_FAILURES FAILURE(S)"
  TOTAL_FAIL=$((TOTAL_FAIL + CONFLICT_FAILURES))
fi
echo ""

---
name: project-headless-desktop-fuse-uat
description: How to run the desktop FUSE app headlessly against the local stack for agent-driven UAT (incl. the macFUSE-vs-FUSE-T linking gotcha)
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: eae1b4bd-fe3d-40ed-9c53-b3dee340c487
---

The desktop FUSE app CAN be driven headlessly by an agent for UAT — no human GUI login needed. Recipe (macOS, validated 2026-06-13 on phase 43):

1. Stack: `docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up -d` (postgres 5432, kubo 5001/8080, redis **host 6380**, someguy 8190, mock-ipns 3001). mock-ipns shows "unhealthy" but works.
2. API: `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api build` + `migration:run`, then `node dist/main.js` with NODE_ENV=test, DB_DATABASE=cipherbox, REDIS_PORT=6380, DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL=http://localhost:3001, TEST_LOGIN_SECRET=e2e-test-secret-ci-only. No IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY needed (ephemeral RS256 when unset & NODE_ENV!=production).
3. Frontend: build the 5 SDK packages, then `pnpm vite build` + `vite preview --port 1420` in apps/desktop (the debug binary loads frontend from :1420).
4. Binary: `cargo build -p cipherbox-desktop --no-default-features --features fuse`, then `install_name_tool -add_rpath /usr/local/lib <binary>`.
5. Launch: `target/debug/cipherbox-desktop --dev-key $(openssl rand -hex 32)` with CIPHERBOX_API_URL + VITE_API_URL + VITE_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET. Headless (webview visible(false)). `--dev-key` value is ignored — it calls `/auth/test-login` (email dev-key@cipherbox.local, deterministic per-email keypair; same vault across restarts). **Must run the launching Bash with `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true`** so the mount syscall/fuse-t helper can run.
6. Mount appears at `~/CipherBox` as `smbfs` (FUSE-T SMB backend, go-nfsv4 process). Use `tests/desktop-e2e/scripts/` (wait-for-mount.sh, test-conflict-detection.sh has a `bump_server_sequence` 409 inducer). Authoritative recipe: `.github/workflows/desktop-e2e.yml`.

GOTCHA (this machine): the debug binary linked **macFUSE** `/usr/local/lib/libfuse.2.dylib` (kext NOT loaded → mount silently never materialises, fuser still logs "mount confirmed") instead of FUSE-T. Both are installed; this machine's `/usr/local/lib/pkgconfig/fuse.pc` is macFUSE's. Fix: make a `fuse.pc` aliased to fuse-t (copy `/Library/Application Support/fuse-t/pkgconfig/fuse-t.pc`, set `Version: 2.9.9`, keep `-lfuse-t`), put its dir FIRST in PKG_CONFIG_PATH, `cargo clean -p fuser cipherbox-fuse cipherbox-desktop`, rebuild. Verify with `otool -L <binary> | grep fuse` → must show `@rpath/libfuse-t.dylib`.

Caveats: test-login access token TTL is **900s (15 min)** — restart the app per test phase or uploads 401. cb-journal lives at `~/Library/Application Support/cipherbox/cb-journal` (mode 0700). Tearing down: kill the app + `diskutil unmount force ~/CipherBox` (it mounts the user's REAL ~/CipherBox path). See [[project-cross-package-dist-staleness]] for the SDK-rebuild-before-consumer pattern.

**CORS gotcha (validated 2026-07-07, phase 69):** the API MUST be started with `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=http://localhost:5173,http://localhost:1420` (matches `desktop-e2e.yml`). Without it, the webview's `fetch` to `/auth/test-login` (origin `:1420`) fails with **"Load failed"** (CORS block, not an HTTP error), so headless auth silently never completes → no vault → no mount. curl-ing `/auth/test-login` directly still works (no Origin header), which masks the cause.

**Clean-reset gotcha (the biggest time-sink):** desktop-e2e sequence state lives in THREE independent layers and a fully-clean run requires resetting ALL of them together — (1) postgres DB (`dropdb/createdb cipherbox_test` + `migration:run`), (2) the client cb-journal `~/Library/Application Support/cipherbox/cb-journal` (holds `rotation-high-water-seq.json` anti-rollback FLOOR store), and (3) Kubo's IPFS datastore (`docker compose ... down -v` to wipe `ipfs_data`). Partial resets desync the IPNS sequence and every read fails: reset DB-only → floor-store rejects the fresh vault (`Sequence regression rejected: floor=N attempted=M`); reset DB+floor but not Kubo → client resolves a stale IPNS seq from Kubo and the fresh DB rejects it (`First publish: embedded sequence must be 1, got N`). Same HKDF-derived root ipns_name across re-inits is why stale state collides. Node/v3 desktop port (phase 69) validated headlessly this way 2026-07-07 — an e2e-caught D-07 write-plane pairing bug (identity keyed by non-portable local ino; fix keys by stored `node_id`) was fixed here; residual cold-Kubo IPNS read-after-write propagation races remain (not a product bug — CI's warm stack is authoritative). See [[project-fuse-cross-client-sync-gated-reresolve]] for the FUSE-T flake class.

# --- Install FUSE driver (needed for both build and test) ---

      - name: Install FUSE-T (macOS)
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          brew install --cask fuse-t
          sudo mkdir -p /usr/local/lib/pkgconfig
          FUSE_T_PC="/Library/Application Support/fuse-t/pkgconfig/fuse-t.pc"
          if [ ! -f "$FUSE_T_PC" ]; then
            FUSE_T_PC=$(find /Library /usr/local /opt/homebrew -name "fuse-t.pc" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
          fi
          if [ -z "$FUSE_T_PC" ] || [ ! -f "$FUSE_T_PC" ]; then
            echo "::error::fuse-t.pc not found after FUSE-T installation"
            exit 1
          fi
          sudo cp "$FUSE_T_PC" /usr/local/lib/pkgconfig/fuse.pc
          sudo sed -i '' 's/^Version:.*/Version: 2.9.9/' /usr/local/lib/pkgconfig/fuse.pc

      - name: Install system dependencies (Linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev \
            libayatana-appindicator3-dev \
            librsvg2-dev \
            libssl-dev \
            libxdo-dev \
            libfuse3-dev \
            fuse3 \
            pkg-config \
            build-essential
          sudo modprobe fuse || true

      - name: Install WinFsp (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: powershell
        run: |
          $url = "https://github.com/winfsp/winfsp/releases/download/v2.1/winfsp-2.1.25156.msi"
          $out = "winfsp.msi"
          $expectedHash = "073A70E00F77423E34BED98B86E600DEF93393BA5822204FAC57A29324DB9F7A"
          Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -OutFile $out
          $actualHash = (Get-FileHash $out -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
          if ($actualHash -ne $expectedHash) { throw "WinFsp MSI hash mismatch: expected $expectedHash, got $actualHash" }
          Start-Process msiexec.exe -ArgumentList "/i","$out","/qn","INSTALLLEVEL=1000" -Wait -NoNewWindow
          # Verify WinFsp installed and add bin to PATH for DLL discovery
          $winfspDir = (Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\WinFsp" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).InstallDir
          if ($winfspDir) {
            Write-Host "WinFsp installed at: $winfspDir"
            $binDir = Join-Path $winfspDir "bin"
            Write-Host "Adding to PATH: $binDir"
            echo "$binDir" | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_PATH -Encoding utf8 -Append
          } else {
            Write-Host "WARNING: WinFsp registry key not found after install"
          }

      # --- Setup Node.js + pnpm (needed for frontend build before cargo) ---

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@0ebf47130e4866e96fce0953f49152a61190b271 # v6.0.9

      - uses: actions/setup-node@48b55a011bda9f5d6aeb4c2d9c7362e8dae4041e # v6.4.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      # --- Build desktop frontend (Tauri embeds from frontendDist) ---

      - name: Build desktop frontend
        run: |
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/crypto build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/core build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api-client build

**Definitively confirmed.** The correlation is exact:

- Rotation of grant-root folder `…002` (SharedGrant) → immediately followed by root owned-walk failures on child `…002`
- Same for `…009` (DeepGrant) and `…00c` (RenameOverwrite)

Each scope-exit rotation republishes the **grant-root folder node (a direct child of root) with `write_sealed: None`**, so every subsequent owned-walk of root fails closed. macOS FUSE-T/SMB re-enumerates directories constantly (607 failed refreshes here) → the rename's path resolution eventually hits it → persistent EACCES. Linux/Windows cache listings and rarely re-walk → they pass.

This is worse than a test flake: after rotation, the write body (carrying `ipns_private_key`) is gone from the published record, so on a fresh mount **`replay.rs` can't recover the signing seed** → the owner permanently loses write access to any rotated subtree. Let me read the publish path to design the write-plane-preserving fix.

- attempt 1 rotation **completed** (line 109), but then destFile (ino 13) read-body unseal fails AES-GCM (line 110) → SMB `open(destFile)` returns EIO (line 113) → rename fails → retry

The bulk of the 122 AES-GCM errors are the background root-refresh ones my fix *unmasked* (same non-fatal outcome as the old "no write_sealed body"). The fatal ones are Part D's retry re-rotation. I need to determine if this is intermittent (run 1 passed by timing luck) or fix-induced. Let me kick off run 3 (post-fix) for a second data point while I study the retry/idempotency path.

2	//! read-key rotation (D-14, SC#8, Plan 70.1-09).
3	//!
4	//! This is the ASSEMBLY job RESEARCH Sharp Question 7.1 describes: every
5	//! method of `cipherbox_sdk::rotation::engine::RotationDeps` maps to an
6	//! existing single-purpose primitive already shipped elsewhere in the
7	//! workspace. The genuinely NEW piece is the key-checkpoint seam plumbing
8	//! (`persist_wrapped_key`/`get_wrapped_key`/`delete_wrapped_key`, D-01/D-03,
9	//! landed in Plan 70.1-08) wired to the combined `JsonSidecarFloorStore`
10	//! (Plan 70.1-03).
11	//!
12	//! # Design: generic over an injectable `RotationTransport` seam
13	//!
14	//! [`FuseRotationDeps`] is generic over [`RotationTransport`] — the
15	//! resolve/fetch/publish trio — so unit tests can inject an in-memory fake
16	//! (mirroring how `crates/sdk`'s own `FakeDeps` fakes the engine's deps)
17	//! without a live `ApiClient`/network round trip. [`ApiClientTransport`] is
18	//! the production implementor, backed by the real
19	//! `cipherbox_api_client::ipns`/`ipfs` primitives.
20	//!
21	//! # Pitfall 7 (CRITICAL) — the 409 conflict-shape mismatch
22	//!
23	//! The engine's [`PublishAttempt::Conflict`] variant requires a fully
24	//! materialized `remote: PublishedNode`, but `cipherbox_api_client::ipns::
25	//! publish_ipns`'s `PublishResult::Conflict` returns ONLY a
26	//! `current_sequence_number` — never the winning record. On a 409,
27	//! [`FuseRotationDeps::publish_with_cas`] performs a follow-up
28	//! `resolve`+`fetch_node` to materialize the REAL remote before returning
29	//! `PublishAttempt::Conflict` — it MUST NEVER fabricate an empty/placeholder
30	//! `PublishedNode` here (a fabricated remote silently breaks the engine's
31	//! CAS-409 concurrent-add merge, T-70.1-22).
32	//!
33	//! # Known limitation — IPNS signing-key sourcing (documented scope decision)
34	//!
35	//! Publishing a rotated node's new IPNS record requires that node's own
36	//! Ed25519 signing seed. RESEARCH's "assembly job" framing does not specify
37	//! a source for this beyond the owner's ECIES keypair (which wraps the
38	//! read-key CHECKPOINT, not IPNS signing material). [`ApiClientTransport`]
39	//! sources the signing seed from the ALREADY-MOUNTED, in-memory
40	//! `InodeTable` (`InodeKind::{Root,Folder,File}.ipns_private_key` — the same
41	//! plaintext-in-memory cache `fs.rs::build_folder_metadata` already reads
42	//! for local publishes). This works for any node the FUSE mount has
43	//! materialized (the common case for a scope-exit rotation, since the owner
44	//! is actively mutating a locally-browsed subtree), and fails CLOSED
45	//! (`Err` -> EIO) for a node not yet locally materialized, rather than
46	//! inventing a parallel write-key-chain-walk mechanism (out of scope per

content.text: This reframes it correctly. **The delete path (Parts A/C) uses `run_scope_exit_gate_coalesced`, which EXCLUDES the removed child from the rotation. The rename dest-gate uses the plain `run_scope_exit_gate`, which INCLUDES destFile** — so the rotation re-keys the very file that's about to be overwritten, and FUSE-T's immediate `open(destFile)` then races the rotated record's IPNS propagation (Linux never opens it → passes). The delete path proves the fix: **exclude the overwritten destination from the rotation, like delete excludes the deleted child.** Let me read the coalesced gate and its delete caller.

699	/// with the POST-delete child list ([`crate::CipherBoxFS::build_scope_exit_child_override`],
700	/// which mutates NO state — fail-closed until the rotation succeeds), so the
701	/// rotation republishes the grant-root as the SINGLE authoritative publish
702	/// (post-delete, new key) and the caller MUST suppress its own parent relink.
703	/// A deep scope-exit, a private delete, or a non-covered mutation returns
704	/// `Ok(false)` and the caller performs its normal relink (now resealed under
705	/// the Fix-A-refreshed key when a rotation ran).
706	///
707	/// Returns:
708	/// - `Ok(true)`  — shallow covered scope-exit coalesced; the caller MUST SKIP
709	///   its plain `update_folder_metadata(parent)` relink.
710	/// - `Ok(false)` — private / deep / non-covered; the caller relinks as normal.
711	/// - `Err(())`   — fail-closed (poisoned cache / D-15a / D-15b / rotation
712	///   failure); the caller maps this to EIO / STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED and aborts.
713	///
714	/// D-07 dual-keying and the D-15a/b/c fail-closed conditions are preserved
715	/// exactly as in [`run_scope_exit_gate`].
716	#[cfg(any(feature = "fuse", feature = "winfsp"))]
717	pub fn run_scope_exit_gate_coalesced(
718	    fs: &mut crate::CipherBoxFS,
719	    child_ino: u64,
720	    parent_ino: u64,
721	) -> Result<bool, ()> {
722	    // Write-plane key (D-07): the mutated node's stable id, kept DISTINCT from
723	    // the read-plane grant-root ipns_name.
724	    let child_id = fs
725	        .inodes
726	        .get(child_ino)
727	        .map(|i| i.node_id.clone())
728	        .unwrap_or_else(|| crate::fs::uuid_from_ino(child_ino));
729	
730	    // Detect coverage under an immutable borrow FIRST (D-15a/b/c fail-closed).
731	    let grant_root_ipns_name = match detect_scope_exit_grant_root(fs, child_ino)? {
732	        None => return Ok(false),
733	        Some(name) => name,
734	    };
735	
736	    // Shallow scope-exit? (the grant-root IS the deleted node's direct parent).
737	    // If so, build the post-delete child list WITHOUT mutating state (the child
738	    // inode is only removed after the rotation succeeds — fail-closed) and drive
739	    // the coalesced single publish.
740	    let parent_ipns = fs
741	        .inodes
742	        .get(parent_ino)
743	        .map(|p| match &p.kind {
744	            InodeKind::Root { ipns_name, .. } | InodeKind::Folder { ipns_name, .. } => {
745	                ipns_name.clone()
746	            }
747	            _ => String::new(),
748	        })
749	        .unwrap_or_default();
750	    let root_children_override = if !parent_ipns.is_empty() && parent_ipns == grant_root_ipns_name {
751	        // Fail closed: an incomplete override would drop children from the
752	        // grant-root's republished read plane (silent orphaning), so a build
753	        // failure aborts the whole scope-exit rather than publishing a short list.
754	        match fs.build_scope_exit_child_override(parent_ino, child_ino) {
755	            Ok(children) => Some(children),
756	            Err(e) => {
757	                log::error!(
758	                    "scope-exit coalesced child override failed (fail-closed): {}",
759	                    e
760	                );
761	                return Err(());
762	            }
763	        }
764	    } else {
765	        None
766	    };
767	    let coalesced = root_children_override.is_some();
768	
769	    let rt = fs.rt.clone();
770	    rt.block_on(rotate_read_on_scope_exit(
771	        fs,
772	        &grant_root_ipns_name,
773	        &child_id,
774	        root_children_override,
775	    ))
776	    .map(|()| coalesced)
777	    .map_err(|e| {
778	        log::error!("scope-exit gate failed (fail-closed): {}", e);
779	    })
780	}

content.text:
**Breakthrough — I had the target backwards.** Mapping run 6's inodes:
- destFile = ino 12 (attempt 1's `child_ino=12`); the override **correctly excludes it** (`coalesced=true, override_len=1`).
- The single override child = ino 13 = **sourceFile** — the SURVIVING node, which the rotation rotates. `rotate_one` and the `open`/AES-GCM failures are all on **ino 13 (sourceFile)**.

So FUSE-T's overwrite-rename opens the **source** file (to move it); the source is a surviving child that the rotation re-keys, and the immediate open re-resolves it from IPNS before propagation → AES-GCM/EIO → EACCES. Linux never opens the source → passes. Excluding the destination can't help. Let me check whether a file upload marks its inode resolved (so `open` avoids the IPNS re-resolve entirely).

content.text: `UploadComplete` (fs.rs:463-464) *does* set the inode's cid — so after upload, sourceFile should be locally resolved and `open` should skip the IPNS re-resolve. Yet `open(ino 13)` still re-resolves (cid empty). A background metadata refresh (`apply_owned_children`) likely re-materializes the file with an empty cid, clobbering it. And critically: **Phase 74's SC1 (74-03) is what ADDED file rotation** — before it, files weren't rotated in a scope-exit, so this couldn't happen. That makes Part D a Phase-74 regression, consistent with "failing the entire branch lifetime." Let me confirm how `apply_owned_children` materializes a File's cid.

content.text:
Here's where I've landed after reproducing it 6 times locally (macOS FUSE-T, full stack). It **consistently fails**, matching your read exactly — and I can now explain precisely why it's macOS-only.

## Root cause (confirmed, and it's a Phase 74 regression)

**Phase 74's SC1 (`74-03`) added *file* read-key rotation to scope-exit** (`mint_file_key_on_rotate` — before it, only folders rotated). The Part-D overwrite-rename scope-exit rotates the **surviving source file** (it must — to cut off the revoked recipient). Rotating it re-keys + republishes its node.

Then the macOS-only trigger: **FUSE-T/SMB's overwrite-rename `open()`s the *source* file** to move it. Linux's kernel `rename` never opens the source — which is exactly why the identical test passes on Linux. That `open` re-resolves the just-rotated file from IPNS and gets a record whose key doesn't match the inode's freshly-rotated key → `AES-GCM decryption failed` → EIO → the whole rename `EACCES`es. Then each of the 6 retries re-runs the scope-exit rotation on the **already-rotated** subtree, which fails `verify_subtree_clean` (same reason) — so it never recovers.

I proved the inode mapping with debug logging: the gate correctly identifies destFile vs sourceFile; the failing `open`/`rotate_one` are all on the **source** file (ino 13), the surviving child.

## Why it's not a quick fix (3 attempts, none passed)

1. **Preserve `write_sealed` on rotation** — fixed a *real* separate durability bug (607→0 "no write_sealed body"), but not this; reverted.
2. **`open`/`read` self-heal: re-resolve with the current key** — the re-resolve *also* got AES-GCM (the served record itself is stale/key-mismatched, not just a stale captured key); reverted.
3. **Coalesced dest-gate (exclude the destination from rotation, like `unlink` does)** — verified it excludes destFile correctly, but the failure is the **source** file, which *must* survive and rotate; reverted.

The deep reason all three fall short: for these nodes the resolve is racing **IPNS eventual consistency**. `ipns.service.ts` stores the full record in the DB on publish and *claims* to prefer DB, but the `seqFloor` shared-folder branch (lines 704–727) serves the **network/someguy** record (~10–30s DHT lag). So a just-rotated shared-folder node isn't immediately resolvable — and FUSE-T reads it immediately.

## Recommendation

The clean fix is to make the **owner's resolve of their own shared-folder nodes read-after-write consistent** (prefer the DB record the publish just wrote, instead of the lagging network record). That removes the race for *all three* symptoms at once (source `open`, owned-walk refresh, and the retry re-rotation) rather than papering over one. It's likely a small change in the resolve reconciliation, but I want to **confirm with one instrumented run** whether these file nodes are actually being served from network vs DB before I touch the API resolve path — I don't want to guess at a crypto/resolve seam.

My local stack is still up and warm, so iteration is now just build+run (~10 min each).

How do you want me to proceed?

content.text:
The `RESOLVE-DEBUG` confirmation is decisive — and it **refutes** the API-lag theory (good call to verify before touching the resolve path):

- **596 `normal` rows, 0 `seqFloor`** across the whole run. None of these nodes use the network/DHT-lag path.
- The failing source file was served **DB-preferred at the correct sequence** (`cachedType=normal, networkSeq=2, dbSeqOrFloor=2`). The API hands the client the current, just-published record.

So the resolve is read-after-write consistent. **The bug is entirely client-side.** The `AES-GCM decryption failed` is a *key* mismatch, not a stale *record*: the rotation's `rotate_one` derives the file's key from the parent grant-root's child-ref, but the file's own (correctly-served) record is sealed with a *different* key. The parent's child-ref and the child's own record have diverged.

The most likely mechanism, given the evidence: attempt 1's rename fails on the FUSE-T source-`open`, but its scope-exit rotation **partially lands** (grant-root republished / child-refs updated) before failing — leaving the parent's child-ref key and the child's own record key inconsistent. Every one of the 6 retries then re-runs the rotation over that inconsistent subtree and fails `rotate_one`/`verify_subtree_clean`, so it never recovers. The FUSE-T trigger (opening the source file, which Linux never does) is still what kicks off attempt 1's failure.

**Net:** this is a client rotation-atomicity/concurrency bug exposed by FUSE-T, not the API, and not the three things I already tried. Pinning the exact divergence point needs one more instrumented run logging the actual key fingerprints (parent-derived key vs the file record's key, per attempt) — that will show definitively whether it's the partial-rotation-then-retry cascade or a concurrent per-file republish racing the rotation, and points at the precise fix (make the rename's gate atomic/idempotent, or refresh the child inode key before the source-open).

content.text: **Root cause pinned.** The `file-unseal-FAIL` at line 259 — *immediately after* attempt 1's rotation "completed" — uses key `f78882d5` (the file's **original**, pre-rotation key), while the rotation just published the file at `37bc7281`. So **`refresh_rotated_inode_read_keys` did not update this file's inode to the rotated key** (it's a depth-2 file under `…400b` under grant-root `…400c`). The stale inode key then feeds a background parent republish that overwrites the rotation's consistent child-ref → parent (`f78882d5`) and file (`37bc7281`) diverge → every retry's `rotate_one` fails. Let me instrument `refresh_rotated_inode_read_keys` to confirm the file is (or isn't) in `rotated_nodes` and whether its inode gets updated.

content.text:
**Bug #1 confirmed precisely (line 282 vs 285):** refresh correctly sets the file's inode to `608bfef7`, but a **stale in-flight FilePointer resolution** (spawned before the rotation, capturing the old key `47cef7a7`) completes and fails — and the `open` sees that failure and returns EIO, even though the inode now holds the correct key. That fails attempt 1 → retry → the re-rotation bug (#2) cascades.

The fix is the self-heal I attempted earlier, but done correctly: my run-4 version only re-spawned if *nothing* was in-flight at poll start — so when the stale resolution failed *during* the poll, it returned EIO without re-resolving. It must re-spawn with the **current (refreshed) inode key** after a failure. Let me revert all debug instrumentation and implement it properly.

Still failing — and importantly, the self-heal ran 18× but the fresh re-resolve with the current inode key **also** failed. So the problem isn't just a stale captured key: the published data itself is inconsistent. Combined with run 9's evidence (attempt 2 derives the file's *original* key), this reveals the true mechanism:

**After attempt 1's rotation publishes the file + parent child-ref consistently at the new key and refreshes the inode, a concurrent background folder-republish (the rename's `update_folder_metadata`, running against the publish coordinator) re-publishes the parent — and because `refresh_rotated_inode_read_keys` runs *after* the rotation's publishes, that concurrent republish can reintroduce the pre-rotation child-ref key, reverting the parent. Now the parent's child-ref and the file's own record disagree, so every retry's `rotate_one` fails, and no read-path retry can fix inconsistent published data.**

So my read-path self-heal is the wrong layer. Let me revert it and report — this is a rotation-engine/publish-coordinator atomicity bug, not a read-path one.

title: macOS FUSE-T covered overwrite-rename fails — scope-exit rotation vs concurrent republish/refresh race (Phase 74 SC1 regression)
area: desktop-fuse-rotation
severity: high
source: Desktop-E2E `shared-scope-exit-rotation.mts` Part D — consistently RED on macOS since Phase 74; PASSES on Linux + Windows. Root-caused locally over 10 full reproductions (macOS FUSE-T, full stack).
files:
  - crates/fuse/src/write_ops/implementation/rename.rs
  - crates/fuse/src/write_ops/grant_scope.rs
  - crates/sdk/src/rotation/engine.rs
  - crates/fuse/src/fs.rs
  - crates/fuse/src/poll.rs
resolves_phase: null
---

## Symptom

`Part D` of the desktop-e2e shared-scope-exit rotation test (a covered
**overwrite-rename**: `renameSync(sourceFile → destFile)` inside a shared
folder) fails **only on macOS**, every time; Linux and Windows pass the
identical test. The client `renameSync` returns `EACCES` after 6 retries.
Parts A/B/C (scope-exit via `unlink`) pass on macOS.

## Why it's macOS-only (confirmed)

FUSE-T/SMB's overwrite-rename **`open()`s the source file** as part of its
sequence. Linux's kernel `rename` never opens the source. So only macOS reads
a just-rotated file immediately after the scope-exit rotation.

## Root cause (confirmed with key-fingerprint instrumentation)

Phase 74 SC1 (`74-03`) added **file** read-key rotation to scope-exit (before

2. **Concurrent republish reverts the parent child-ref** — the rotation

   `refresh_rotated_inode_read_keys` runs AFTER the publishes. A concurrent
   background folder republish (debounced publisher / the rename's

   re-publish the parent's child-ref at the PRE-rotation key, reverting it.

content.text:
**Root cause fully pinned (line 244 → 270 → 272):**
- Setup published the grant root (folder 11) with child 13 @ original key `3f20fe46` (line 244), triggering an in-flight metadata refresh.
- Rotation completed at 16:10:43 (line 270) — rotated child 13 to a new key + refreshed the inode.
- **Immediately after, a stale in-flight metadata refresh completes and `apply_owned_children` re-materializes ino 13 back to the *original* `3f20fe46`** (line 272, `reuse=true`) — clobbering the rotation's refresh. A subsequent grant-root republish then uses the reset key, reverting the parent → divergence → retries fail.

So the fix is: **a stale metadata refresh must not downgrade a just-rotated inode's key.** Let me look at the refresh-completion apply path to find where to gate it.

---
name: project-fuse-scope-exit-rotation-stale-refresh-clobber
description: Why a FUSE scope-exit read-key rotation must mark its rotated folders as mutated_folders (stale-refresh clobber that broke macOS FUSE-T overwrite-rename)
metadata:
  type: project
---

A FUSE scope-exit read-key rotation (`crates/fuse/src/write_ops/grant_scope.rs::rotate_read_on_scope_exit`) MUST add its rotated FOLDER inodes to `fs.mutated_folders` right after `refresh_rotated_inode_read_keys`. It republishes those folders out-of-band (via the rotation engine, not the mount publish queue), so without this they were never recorded as locally-changed — and a STALE in-flight metadata refresh (one that resolved a PRE-rotation snapshot but completes AFTER the rotation) clobbers the freshly-refreshed inode keys via `apply_owned_children`, resetting them to pre-rotation values. A later parent republish then uses the reset key and reverts the grant-root's child-refs → the parent's child-ref key and the child's own record key diverge → every subsequent `rotate_one`/`verify_subtree_clean` fails AES-GCM (fail-closed). `drain_refresh_completions` (fs.rs) ALREADY guards `mutated_folders`/`publish_queue` against exactly this folder-state desync (it runs `mark_remotely_edited_files_unresolved`, which PRESERVES keys, instead of `apply_owned_children`); a rotation is a local mutation of those folders, so it belongs in that set (30s TTL).

**Symptom this fixed:** desktop-e2e `shared-scope-exit-rotation.mts` **Part D** (covered overwrite-`rename`) failed on macOS EVERY run since Phase 74, passed on Linux+Windows. macOS-only because FUSE-T/SMB's overwrite-rename `open()`s the SOURCE file (Linux's kernel `rename` never does), reading the just-rotated file and tripping the divergence. Phase 74 SC1 (`74-03`) introduced FILE rotation, which is what made rotated files readable-and-clobberable. Fix = ~20 lines in `grant_scope.rs`; verified 3/3 clean local repros (all of rotFAILED/AES-GCM/openEIO signals → 0, vs 5/16/6 before). See [[project-headless-desktop-fuse-uat]] for the local FUSE-T repro recipe and [[project-fuse-cross-client-sync-gated-reresolve]] for the FUSE-T class.

**Ruled out (don't re-chase):** the API resolve is read-after-write consistent (all `normal` DB rows, DB-preferred; instrumented — NOT DHT/seqFloor lag); a read-path `open` self-heal (re-resolve with current inode key) is insufficient because the *published data itself* diverges; `write_sealed:None` on rotation republish is a SEPARATE real durability bug (breaks owned-walks + replay signing-seed recovery, 607→0 "no write_sealed body" when preserved) worth landing on its own but NOT the Part D cause; excluding the rename DESTINATION from rotation (coalesced dest-gate) can't help because the failing node is the surviving SOURCE.

---
created: 2026-07-11T00:00:00.000Z
title: Read-key rotation republishes rotated nodes with write_sealed=None — breaks owned-walks + replay signing-seed recovery
area: desktop-fuse-rotation
severity: high
source: Found while root-causing the macOS Part-D overwrite-rename failure (2026-07-11). Separate, orthogonal bug — NOT the Part-D cause (that was the stale-refresh clobber, fixed inline). Prototyped a fix (607→0 "no write_sealed body") and reverted to keep the Part-D fix minimal.
files:
  - crates/fuse/src/write_ops/rotation_deps.rs
  - crates/sdk/src/rotation/engine.rs
  - crates/sdk/src/listing.rs
  - crates/fuse/src/replay.rs
resolves_phase: null
---

## Problem

A scope-exit read-key rotation republishes every rotated node with
`write_sealed: None` — the engine (`engine.rs::seal_and_publish`, ~2 sites)
never populates it (read-key rotation is a read-plane op), and the FUSE
adapter (`rotation_deps.rs`, documented as a Phase-72 deferral) doesn't
reconstruct it either. Consequences:

- Any `list_folder_owned` over a folder containing a rotated node fails closed
  ("owned child … has no write_sealed body"). On the OWNER's mount this makes
  the background root/folder metadata refresh permanently fail for any
  shared-folder subtree that has been scope-exit-rotated (observed 607×
  "no write_sealed body" per run on macOS; folder-refresh WARN, non-fatal but
  the folder listing never refreshes).
- On a fresh mount, `replay.rs` cannot recover the node's signing seed (the
  seed lives in the write body) — a DURABILITY hole: after a rotation +
  remount the owner may lose the ability to sign updates to the rotated
  subtree.

## Fix (prototyped, verified, reverted)

Preserve the write plane on the rotation republish: in
`ApiClientTransport::publish` (rotation_deps.rs), when `node.write_sealed` is
`None`, reconstruct it from the mount's in-memory InodeTable (the node's own
stable write key + `ipns_private_key` + child `WriteChildRef`s rebuilt from the
child inodes — child write keys are read-key-rotation-independent) and re-seal
`NodeWriteBody` under the node's write key at the node's NEW generation via
`seal_node` (which shares the ROLE_BODY AAD with `seal_published_node`'s
write-body path). Round-trips: unseal under the write key at the new generation
recovers the write body + child refs. Fails-open to `None` for a node not
locally materialized (matches the existing signing-seed fail-closed lookup).
Verified locally: the "no write_sealed body" flood drops 607→0.

Write-key *rotation* remains a separate Phase-72 concern; this only re-seals the
UNCHANGED write plane at the bumped generation. Add unit tests for the
reconstruction round-trip + the None fallback (were written in the prototype).

content.text:
Fixed and verified. Here's the summary.

## Result: macOS Part D now passes deterministically (3/3)

Before the fix: **7 consecutive failures**. After: **3/3 clean passes**, every failure signature zeroed (`rotFAILED:0, AES-GCM:0, openEIO:0` — was 5/16/6), and the SC3 security invariant holds (Frank cut off, Grace re-minted).

## Root cause (fully instrumented)

A FUSE scope-exit read-key rotation republishes its folders **out-of-band** via the rotation engine, so it never recorded them as locally mutated. That let a **stale in-flight metadata refresh** — one that resolved a *pre-rotation* snapshot but completed *after* the rotation — clobber the freshly-refreshed inode keys via `apply_owned_children`. A later parent republish then used the reset key, reverting the grant-root's child-refs → the parent's child-ref key and the child's own record key diverged → every retry's `rotate_one`/`verify_subtree_clean` failed AES-GCM, so the rename never landed. macOS-only because FUSE-T/SMB's overwrite-rename `open()`s the **source** file (Linux's kernel `rename` doesn't), reading the just-rotated file and tripping it. It's a Phase-74 SC1 (`74-03`, file rotation) regression.

## The fix (`crates/fuse/src/write_ops/grant_scope.rs`, +38 lines)

After a rotation refreshes inode keys, **mark the rotated folders as `mutated_folders`**. `drain_refresh_completions` *already* guards that set against exactly this folder-state desync (it runs `mark_remotely_edited_files_unresolved`, which preserves keys, instead of `apply_owned_children`) — a rotation is a local mutation of those folders, so it belongs there. Minimal, reuses existing tested infrastructure, platform-agnostic (safe for Linux/Windows, which already pass).

Verification: `cargo test -p cipherbox-fuse` 117/117; desktop-e2e rotation suite 3/3 local (macOS FUSE-T). CI's `Cargo Check & Test (Windows)` + Linux/Windows desktop-e2e will confirm the shared-code build.

## Also captured (not the Part-D cause, so not applied here)

- Todo: **rotation republishes `write_sealed:None`** — a real durability bug (owned-walks fail; replay can't recover the signing seed). Prototyped a fix (607→0 "no write_sealed body"), reverted to keep this change minimal.
- Memory + ruled-out list (API resolve is consistent; read-path self-heal insufficient; coalesced dest-gate can't help) recorded so it isn't re-chased.

Tree is clean except the fix + the new todo; shared docker stack left running (only the session's desktop/API/mount stopped).

**This is the fix that unblocks PR #607's Desktop-E2E gate.** Want me to commit it to the Phase 74 branch and push to PR #607 (with `git fetch`+rebase first for the release bot)?

created: 2026-07-11T00:00:00.000Z
title: Read-key rotation republishes rotated nodes with write_sealed=None — breaks owned-walks + replay signing-seed recovery
area: desktop-fuse-rotation
severity: high
source: Found while root-causing the macOS Part-D overwrite-rename failure (2026-07-11). Separate, orthogonal bug — NOT the Part-D cause (that was the stale-refresh clobber, fixed inline). Prototyped a fix (607→0 "no write_sealed body") and reverted to keep the Part-D fix minimal.
files:
  - crates/fuse/src/write_ops/rotation_deps.rs
  - crates/sdk/src/rotation/engine.rs
  - crates/sdk/src/listing.rs
  - crates/fuse/src/replay.rs
resolves_phase: null
---

## Problem

A scope-exit read-key rotation republishes every rotated node with
`write_sealed: None` — the engine (`engine.rs::seal_and_publish`, ~2 sites)
never populates it (read-key rotation is a read-plane op), and the FUSE
adapter (`rotation_deps.rs`, documented as a Phase-72 deferral) doesn't
reconstruct it either. Consequences:

- Any `list_folder_owned` over a folder containing a rotated node fails closed
  ("owned child … has no write_sealed body"). On the OWNER's mount this makes
  the background root/folder metadata refresh permanently fail for any
  shared-folder subtree that has been scope-exit-rotated (observed 607×
  "no write_sealed body" per run on macOS; folder-refresh WARN, non-fatal but
  the folder listing never refreshes).
- On a fresh mount, `replay.rs` cannot recover the node's signing seed (the
  seed lives in the write body) — a DURABILITY hole: after a rotation +
  remount the owner may lose the ability to sign updates to the rotated
  subtree.

## Fix (prototyped, verified, reverted)

Preserve the write plane on the rotation republish: in
`ApiClientTransport::publish` (rotation_deps.rs), when `node.write_sealed` is
`None`, reconstruct it from the mount's in-memory InodeTable (the node's own
stable write key + `ipns_private_key` + child `WriteChildRef`s rebuilt from the
child inodes — child write keys are read-key-rotation-independent) and re-seal
`NodeWriteBody` under the node's write key at the node's NEW generation via
`seal_node` (which shares the ROLE_BODY AAD with `seal_published_node`'s
write-body path). Round-trips: unseal under the write key at the new generation
recovers the write body + child refs. Fails-open to `None` for a node not
locally materialized (matches the existing signing-seed fail-closed lookup).
Verified locally: the "no write_sealed body" flood drops 607→0.

Write-key *rotation* remains a separate Phase-72 concern; this only re-seals the
UNCHANGED write plane at the bumped generation. Add unit tests for the
reconstruction round-trip + the None fallback (were written in the prototype).

name: project-fuse-scope-exit-rotation-stale-refresh-clobber
description: Why a FUSE scope-exit read-key rotation must mark its rotated folders as mutated_folders (stale-refresh clobber that broke macOS FUSE-T overwrite-rename)
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 483e60b7-fc2f-4754-bb13-36a935f407c4
---

A FUSE scope-exit read-key rotation (`crates/fuse/src/write_ops/grant_scope.rs::rotate_read_on_scope_exit`) MUST add its rotated FOLDER inodes to `fs.mutated_folders` right after `refresh_rotated_inode_read_keys`. It republishes those folders out-of-band (via the rotation engine, not the mount publish queue), so without this they were never recorded as locally-changed — and a STALE in-flight metadata refresh (one that resolved a PRE-rotation snapshot but completes AFTER the rotation) clobbers the freshly-refreshed inode keys via `apply_owned_children`, resetting them to pre-rotation values. A later parent republish then uses the reset key and reverts the grant-root's child-refs → the parent's child-ref key and the child's own record key diverge → every subsequent `rotate_one`/`verify_subtree_clean` fails AES-GCM (fail-closed). `drain_refresh_completions` (fs.rs) ALREADY guards `mutated_folders`/`publish_queue` against exactly this folder-state desync (it runs `mark_remotely_edited_files_unresolved`, which PRESERVES keys, instead of `apply_owned_children`); a rotation is a local mutation of those folders, so it belongs in that set (30s TTL).

**Symptom this fixed:** desktop-e2e `shared-scope-exit-rotation.mts` **Part D** (covered overwrite-`rename`) failed on macOS EVERY run since Phase 74, passed on Linux+Windows. macOS-only because FUSE-T/SMB's overwrite-rename `open()`s the SOURCE file (Linux's kernel `rename` never does), reading the just-rotated file and tripping the divergence. Phase 74 SC1 (`74-03`) introduced FILE rotation, which is what made rotated files readable-and-clobberable. Fix = ~20 lines in `grant_scope.rs`; verified 3/3 clean local repros (all of rotFAILED/AES-GCM/openEIO signals → 0, vs 5/16/6 before). See [[project-headless-desktop-fuse-uat]] for the local FUSE-T repro recipe and [[project-fuse-cross-client-sync-gated-reresolve]] for the FUSE-T class.

**Ruled out (don't re-chase):** the API resolve is read-after-write consistent (all `normal` DB rows, DB-preferred; instrumented — NOT DHT/seqFloor lag); a read-path `open` self-heal (re-resolve with current inode key) is insufficient because the *published data itself* diverges; `write_sealed:None` on rotation republish is a SEPARATE real durability bug (breaks owned-walks + replay signing-seed recovery, 607→0 "no write_sealed body" when preserved) worth landing on its own but NOT the Part D cause; excluding the rename DESTINATION from rotation (coalesced dest-gate) can't help because the failing node is the surviving SOURCE.

skills.content:
# Ship Phase

Run the full post-`execute-phase` loop for a GSD phase **autonomously, without babysitting**:
verify → secure → validate → simplify → **SDK E2E gate** → CodeRabbit CLI → ship → resolve PR reviews.

Phase number: `74` (e.g. `51`). If empty, infer it from the current branch / latest `.planning/phases/<N>-*` with executed plans.

## Operating rules (so this needs no babysitting)

- **Decide, don't ask.** For every review/audit finding, pick exactly one of **three** dispositions and proceed. The default for anything that isn't clearly material is **discard**, not defer — the todo backlog is a signal for real upcoming work, so keep it small.
  - **Fix now** — the finding is a genuine bug, security/privacy issue, or correctness gap **AND** (it's in the phase's domain OR the fix is small and safe). Always fix real defects the phase itself introduced, regardless of size, or block on them if you can't.
  - **Log a todo** — defer to `.planning/todos/pending/` **only if the item clears the materiality bar**: it's a real defect or a concrete, actionable piece of future work with a plausible owner phase, that you are choosing not to do now because it's out of domain, risky, or large. Before writing one, **search existing pending todos and dedupe** — append to or skip a near-duplicate rather than adding a new file. Note logged todos in the PR.
  - **Discard** — do nothing and do not create a todo. This is the right call for: style/naming/formatting nits, subjective preferences, speculative "could hypothetically" findings with no demonstrated impact, micro-optimizations, test-only suggestions of marginal value, and low-severity **pre-existing** noise unrelated to the phase. Briefly acknowledge dismissed classes in the PR (e.g. "N nits dismissed") rather than filing them.
  - **Materiality bar for a todo** (must meet at least one): user-visible or data-integrity impact; security/privacy/crypto relevance; a real crash/correctness risk; or a concrete follow-up a future phase will genuinely need. "A reviewer mentioned it" is not sufficient. When unsure whether an item clears the bar, **discard it** — a missed low-value item is cheaper than backlog noise.
  - Only stop for: a real failing gate you cannot fix, a genuine ambiguity in intent, or the final merge decision.
- **Verify outcomes faithfully.** Quote real test output. Never report a step done that wasn't.
- Run independent checks in parallel. Keep yourself as orchestrator; hand large self-contained chunks to sub-agents (Rust builds, mechanical sweeps) and adversarially verify their results.

## Environment gotchas (apply throughout)

- Prefix every GitHub CLI call with `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh …`.
- **`git push` / `git fetch` are blocked in the sandbox this environment** — run them with the sandbox disabled. Plain `gh api` reads/writes work sandboxed.
- The commit helper can report `commit_failed` while the commit actually lands — **verify with `git log --oneline -1`, never blindly retry**.
- `gh pr edit` fails on this repo (Projects-classic GraphQL) — patch the body via `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/<N> -F body=@file`.
- PR title + commit subjects: **conventional, no parentheses in the subject** (commitlint + `lint-pr-title` CI reject parens). Escape bare `#NN` item refs as `` `#NN` `` in PR bodies (GFM autolinks them).
- `markdownlint` runs on commit but **excludes `.planning/`** — don't lint files there; prettier still runs.
- After `gh pr create` and after a passing Release Preview, `github-actions[bot]` pushes a `chore(release)` commit to the branch — **`git fetch` + rebase before the next push** or it's rejected.

## Steps

### 1. Verify

Invoke `/gsd-verify-work 74`. Must reach a PASS verdict (`<phase>-VERIFICATION.md`). Fix real gaps; re-run.

### 2. Secure

Invoke `/gsd-secure-phase 74`. Must reach SECURED (`<phase>-SECURITY.md`). If the auditor writes to repo-root `SECURITY.md`, `git restore` it and write the phase doc instead.

### 2b. Crypto/privacy review (conditional)

**Only when the phase touched crypto- or privacy-adjacent code.** Check the phase diff for the signal before deciding:

```bash
git diff origin/main...HEAD --name-only | grep -iE 'crypt|cipher|encrypt|decrypt|key|ecies|aes|gcm|ipns|tee|web3auth|nonce|iv|seal|zeroiz|privacy' | grep -vE '\.test\.|__tests__|\.md$'
```

If that surfaces nothing relevant, **skip this step** and note "no crypto/privacy-adjacent changes" in the PR. Otherwise invoke `/crypto-privacy-review` scoped to the phase code (its `Phase code` scope, or the changed files), triage findings with the three-way operating rule (fix real crypto/privacy defects now, log a todo only for material deferrals, discard nits), and reference the resulting `.planning/security/REVIEW-*.md` in the PR body. This is a deeper crypto lens on top of the `/gsd-secure-phase` threat-model audit, not a replacement for it.

### 2c. Built-in security review

Invoke Claude Code's built-in `/security-review` on the phase diff (`origin/main...HEAD`) — a general vulnerability sweep (injection, authz, secrets, unsafe deserialization, etc.) that complements the crypto-focused passes above. Triage each finding with the three-way operating rule (fix real vulnerabilities now, log a todo only for material deferrals, discard nits/false positives). Note the disposition in the PR body.

### 3. Validate (Nyquist)

Invoke `/gsd-validate-phase 74`. Must be compliant, 0 gaps (`<phase>-VALIDATION.md`).

### 4. Simplify

Review the phase diff (`git diff origin/main...HEAD`) for over-engineering, duplication, and dead code. Apply safe simplifications; log a todo for a larger refactor only if it clears the materiality bar, otherwise discard it.

### 5. SDK E2E gate — DO NOT SKIP

This is the **only** suite that exercises the real client→API IPNS publish/resolve round-trip; unit suites mock the boundary and miss integration regressions (this gate caught a 48/89 break in Phase 51). Run it locally whenever the phase touched IPNS publish/resolve, sequencing/CAS, or key lifecycle:

```bash
# prereqs usually already up: postgres 5432, kubo 5001, redis 6380, mock-ipns-routing 3001
# rebuild the client chain so dist matches CI:
pnpm --filter @cipherbox/crypto build && pnpm --filter @cipherbox/core build \
  && pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api-client build && pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk-core build \
  && pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk build && pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api build
# (re)start the API on :3000 (kill anything already there first):
lsof -nP -iTCP:3000 -sTCP:LISTEN -t | xargs -r kill -9
( cd apps/api && PORT=3000 node dist/main.js > /tmp/ship-phase-api.log 2>&1 & )
# wait for /health, then run the suite:
SDK_E2E_API_URL=http://localhost:3000 \
  SDK_E2E_SECRET="$(grep -E '^TEST_LOGIN_SECRET=' apps/api/.env | cut -d= -f2-)" \
  THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET="$(grep -E '^THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET=' apps/api/.env | cut -d= -f2-)" \
  pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk-e2e test
```

Must be all green. The API does **not** log handled 4xx — to find a real 400 reason, temporarily add an axios response interceptor in `packages/api-client/src/instance.ts` logging `err.response.data`, rebuild the client chain, run one suite, then revert. Shut the API down when done.

### 6. CodeRabbit CLI review (local, before ship)

```bash
coderabbit review --agent --base main --type committed
```

Triage every finding with the three-way operating rule above (fix / log a material todo / discard). Re-run until the in-scope set is clean. For the deferrals that clear the materiality bar, capture todos with file refs + the right destination phase; discard the nits.

### 7. Conventional-commit reword

GSD executor commits use a non-conventional `feat 51-03:` style that fails the `pr-release-preview` CI gate on any commit touching versioned packages. Reword the phase's commit subjects to conventional **before** opening the PR:

```bash
git filter-branch --msg-filter 'sed -E "1 s/^([a-z]+) [0-9][0-9A-Za-z.-]*: /\1: /"' <base>..HEAD
```

(`git rebase -i` is not available here.) Verify the tree is unchanged (`git diff <old-head>`), then force-push (sandbox disabled) and clean up the filter-branch backup ref.

### 8. Ship

Invoke `/gsd-ship 74`, but:

- Override the default PR title (GSD's `Phase N: <slug>` is non-conventional) with a conventional, paren-free subject, e.g. `fix: <concise phase summary>`.
- Write the PR body to a temp file (escape `#NN`, end with the Claude Code attribution line) and set it via `gh api -X PATCH` (not `gh pr edit`).
- Push with the sandbox disabled.

### 9. Resolve PR reviews

When CodeRabbit's PR-level review lands (poll `gh pr checks <N>` until the `CodeRabbit` check is no longer pending — use a backgrounded poll, don't block):

- CodeRabbit bundles findings in the **review body** AND as inline **review threads**. Fetch threads via the GraphQL `reviewThreads` query (id, isResolved, path, line, first comment body). Expect it to **re-review your own fix commits** and raise new findings — triage those too.
- For each finding apply the three-way operating rule (fix → reference the commit; material defer → reference the todo; nit → resolve the thread with a brief "acknowledged, not actionable" reply, no todo).
- Then run `/resolve-pr-reviews`, or directly: reply to each thread (`addPullRequestReviewThreadReply`) with the disposition and resolve it (`resolveReviewThread`). GitHub's API is occasionally flaky — wrap mutations in a small retry loop and re-query `reviewThreads` afterward to confirm **0 unresolved** and no duplicate replies.
- After any further push, `git fetch` + rebase first (the release bot may have pushed `chore(release)`).

### 10. Confirm green & report

Poll `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh pr checks <N>` until all checks settle. Report: final commit SHA, CI status (all green / which failed), threads resolved (`N/N`), a triage tally (fixed / todos logged / discarded), and the list of deferred todos created. Keep the todos-logged count low — if it's climbing, re-check that each cleared the materiality bar. Leave the merge decision to the user.

### 11. Extract learnings

Invoke `/gsd-extract-learnings 74` to mine the completed phase artifacts for decisions, lessons, patterns, and surprises (writes `<phase>-LEARNINGS.md`). Commit the resulting file on the phase branch alongside the rest of the work — `.planning/` bookkeeping rides the same PR, never a separate docs-only PR.

168	# ---- Test 5: Wait for FUSE mount to pick up edited content ----
169	echo "--- Test 5: Wait for FUSE mount to detect edit ---"
170	# The FUSE mount polls folder metadata every 30s. After detecting a newer
171	# modified_at on the FilePointer, it re-resolves the file's IPNS record
172	# to pick up the new CID. Allow up to 120s for two full polling cycles.
173	SYNC_OK=0
174	for attempt in $(seq 1 24); do
175	  sleep 5
176	  # Trigger readdir to reliably drain refresh completions via
177	  # drain_refresh_completions() -> populate_folder(), which detects
178	  # modified_at changes and marks files for re-resolution. We use `ls`
179	  # here because it is a dependable refresh trigger during polling.
180	  ls "$MP" > /dev/null 2>&1 || true
181	  stat "$MP/$TEST_FILE" > /dev/null 2>&1 || true
182	  FUSE_CONTENT=$(cat "$MP/$TEST_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
183	  if [ "$FUSE_CONTENT" = "$EDITED_CONTENT" ]; then
184	    SYNC_OK=1
185	    echo "  Sync detected on attempt $attempt ($(( attempt * 5 ))s)"
186	    break
187	  fi
188	  echo "  Sync poll attempt $attempt: content still original"
189	done
190	
191	if [ "$SYNC_OK" -eq 1 ]; then
192	  pass "FUSE mount picked up edited content"
193	else
194	  if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ]; then
195	    # Optional on macOS only (mirrors the Test 7 folder-rename leg below).
196	    #
197	    # Root cause is FUSE-T's SMB backend, NOT a sync bug: the desktop's FUSE layer
198	    # correctly detects the remote edit and re-resolves the FilePointer to the new
199	    # CID within ~5s (proven by the crates/fuse drain_refresh_completions unit tests
200	    # and confirmed against a live local mount under RUST_LOG=debug). But the macOS
201	    # SMB client caches the file content above FUSE-T and does not revalidate within
202	    # the window -- it serves the stale read without ever re-calling FUSE `open`. The
203	    # mount is `nonotification` and FUSE-T's SMB backend does NOT honor the FUSE
204	    # `inval_inode` reverse-notification (verified experimentally), so there is no
205	    # reliable FUSE-side way to force the SMB client to drop its cache. It usually
206	    # clears within ~45s but the TTL is variable and intermittently exceeds 120s.
207	    # Linux + Windows (the .ps1) enforce this leg fully; only macOS is downgraded.
208	    # See apps/desktop/CLAUDE.md "FUSE Mount Architecture" for the platform details.
209	    echo "WARN: FUSE mount did not pick up edited content after 120s on macOS (optional)"
210	    echo "  FUSE-T SMB client cache -- not a sync regression; FUSE re-resolves in ~5s."
211	    pass "FUSE content sync (optional on macOS -- timed out, see warning above)"
212	  else
213	    fail "FUSE mount still shows original content after 120s (got: '$FUSE_CONTENT')"
214	  fi
215	fi
216	
217	# ---- Test 6: Rename folder via SDK ----
218	echo "--- Test 6: Rename folder via SDK ---"
219	
220	# 6a. Create a folder with a file inside via FUSE
221	RENAME_DIR="sync-rename-test"
222	RENAMED_DIR="sync-renamed-folder"
223	RENAME_INNER_CONTENT="rename test content"
224	
225	mkdir -p "$MP/$RENAME_DIR"
226	printf '%s' "$RENAME_INNER_CONTENT" > "$MP/$RENAME_DIR/inner.txt"
227	sleep 3
228	# Trigger readdir to flush uploads
229	ls "$MP" > /dev/null 2>&1 || true
230	ls "$MP/$RENAME_DIR" > /dev/null 2>&1 || true
231	
232	# 6b. Wait for the FUSE mount's metadata publish to complete and propagate.
233	# The folder is immediately visible locally, but the IPNS publish takes
234	# 1.5s debounce + publish time. We must wait for this to finish before the
235	# SDK rename, otherwise the FUSE mount's pending publish can overwrite the
236	# SDK's renamed metadata. Verify via SDK rename success (not local stat).
237	RENAME_READY=0
238	RENAME_OK=0
239	echo "  Waiting for FUSE metadata publish to propagate before SDK rename..."
240	for rename_attempt in $(seq 1 12); do
241	  sleep 10
242	  # Trigger readdir to drain publish completions
243	  ls "$MP" > /dev/null 2>&1 || true
244	  if RENAME_OUTPUT=$(run_rename_folder "$RENAME_DIR" "$RENAMED_DIR" 2>&1); then
245	    RENAME_OK=1
246	    echo "  SDK rename succeeded on attempt $rename_attempt ($(( rename_attempt * 10 ))s)"
247	    break
248	  fi
249	  echo "  SDK rename attempt $rename_attempt: folder not yet in remote metadata"
250	done
251	
252	if [ "$RENAME_OK" -eq 1 ]; then
253	  pass "Rename folder via SDK"
254	  echo "  $RENAME_OUTPUT"
255	  RENAME_READY=1
256	else
257	  fail "Rename folder via SDK (not visible in remote metadata after 120s: $RENAME_OUTPUT)"
258	  echo "FATAL: Cannot test folder rename sync without successful rename."
259	fi

# ---- Test 5: Wait for FUSE mount to pick up edited content ----
echo "--- Test 5: Wait for FUSE mount to detect edit ---"
# The FUSE mount polls folder metadata every 30s. After detecting a newer
# modified_at on the FilePointer, it re-resolves the file's IPNS record
# to pick up the new CID. Allow up to 120s for two full polling cycles.
SYNC_OK=0
for attempt in $(seq 1 24); do
  sleep 5
  # Trigger readdir to reliably drain refresh completions via
  # drain_refresh_completions() -> populate_folder(), which detects
  # modified_at changes and marks files for re-resolution. We use `ls`
  # here because it is a dependable refresh trigger during polling.
  ls "$MP" > /dev/null 2>&1 || true
  stat "$MP/$TEST_FILE" > /dev/null 2>&1 || true
  FUSE_CONTENT=$(cat "$MP/$TEST_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  if [ "$FUSE_CONTENT" = "$EDITED_CONTENT" ]; then
    SYNC_OK=1
    echo "  Sync detected on attempt $attempt ($(( attempt * 5 ))s)"
    break
  fi
  echo "  Sync poll attempt $attempt: content still original"
done

if [ "$SYNC_OK" -eq 1 ]; then
  pass "FUSE mount picked up edited content"
else
  if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ]; then
    # Optional on macOS only (mirrors the Test 7 folder-rename leg below).
    #
    # Root cause is FUSE-T's SMB backend, NOT a sync bug: the desktop's FUSE layer
    # correctly detects the remote edit and re-resolves the FilePointer to the new
    # CID within ~5s (proven by the crates/fuse drain_refresh_completions unit tests
    # and confirmed against a live local mount under RUST_LOG=debug). But the macOS
    # SMB client caches the file content above FUSE-T and does not revalidate within
    # the window -- it serves the stale read without ever re-calling FUSE `open`. The
    # mount is `nonotification` and FUSE-T's SMB backend does NOT honor the FUSE
    # `inval_inode` reverse-notification (verified experimentally), so there is no
    # reliable FUSE-side way to force the SMB client to drop its cache. It usually
    # clears within ~45s but the TTL is variable and intermittently exceeds 120s.
    # Linux + Windows (the .ps1) enforce this leg fully; only macOS is downgraded.
    # See apps/desktop/CLAUDE.md "FUSE Mount Architecture" for the platform details.
    echo "WARN: FUSE mount did not pick up edited content after 120s on macOS (optional)"
    echo "  FUSE-T SMB client cache -- not a sync regression; FUSE re-resolves in ~5s."
    pass "FUSE content sync (optional on macOS -- timed out, see warning above)"
  else
    fail "FUSE mount still shows original content after 120s (got: '$FUSE_CONTENT')"
  fi
fi

# ---- Test 6: Rename folder via SDK ----
echo "--- Test 6: Rename folder via SDK ---"

# 6a. Create a folder with a file inside via FUSE
RENAME_DIR="sync-rename-test"
RENAMED_DIR="sync-renamed-folder"
RENAME_INNER_CONTENT="rename test content"

mkdir -p "$MP/$RENAME_DIR"
printf '%s' "$RENAME_INNER_CONTENT" > "$MP/$RENAME_DIR/inner.txt"
sleep 3
# Trigger readdir to flush uploads
ls "$MP" > /dev/null 2>&1 || true
ls "$MP/$RENAME_DIR" > /dev/null 2>&1 || true

# 6b. Wait for the FUSE mount's metadata publish to complete and propagate.
# The folder is immediately visible locally, but the IPNS publish takes
# 1.5s debounce + publish time. We must wait for this to finish before the
# SDK rename, otherwise the FUSE mount's pending publish can overwrite the
# SDK's renamed metadata. Verify via SDK rename success (not local stat).
RENAME_READY=0
RENAME_OK=0
echo "  Waiting for FUSE metadata publish to propagate before SDK rename..."
for rename_attempt in $(seq 1 12); do
  sleep 10
  # Trigger readdir to drain publish completions
  ls "$MP" > /dev/null 2>&1 || true
  if RENAME_OUTPUT=$(run_rename_folder "$RENAME_DIR" "$RENAMED_DIR" 2>&1); then
    RENAME_OK=1
    echo "  SDK rename succeeded on attempt $rename_attempt ($(( rename_attempt * 10 ))s)"
    break
  fi
  echo "  SDK rename attempt $rename_attempt: folder not yet in remote metadata"
done

if [ "$RENAME_OK" -eq 1 ]; then
  pass "Rename folder via SDK"
  echo "  $RENAME_OUTPUT"
  RENAME_READY=1
else
  fail "Rename folder via SDK (not visible in remote metadata after 120s: $RENAME_OUTPUT)"
  echo "FATAL: Cannot test folder rename sync without successful rename."
fi

# ---- Test 7: FUSE mount detects folder rename ----
echo "--- Test 7: Wait for FUSE mount to detect folder rename ---"
if [ "$RENAME_READY" -ne 1 ]; then
  fail "Skipped: folder rename prerequisite failed"
else
  # The FUSE mount polls folder metadata every 30s. After detecting the rename
  # (child entry name changed + modifiedAt bumped), it should show the new
  # folder name and remove the old one. On macOS with FUSE-T's SMB backend,
  # mutated_folders blocking (30s) + cache TTL resets + SMB directory caching
  # can compound delays. Allow up to 300s and treat timeout as optional.
  RENAME_SYNC_OK=0
  for attempt in $(seq 1 60); do
    sleep 5
    # Trigger readdir to drain refresh completions
    ls "$MP" > /dev/null 2>&1 || true
    if [ -d "$MP/$RENAMED_DIR" ] && [ ! -d "$MP/$RENAME_DIR" ]; then
      RENAME_SYNC_OK=1
      echo "  Rename sync detected on attempt $attempt ($(( attempt * 5 ))s)"
      break
    fi
    if [ $(( attempt % 10 )) -eq 0 ]; then
      echo "  Rename sync poll attempt $attempt: not yet renamed"
    fi
  done

  if [ "$RENAME_SYNC_OK" -eq 1 ]; then
    # Verify nested content survived the rename
    INNER_CONTENT=$(cat "$MP/$RENAMED_DIR/inner.txt" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    if [ "$INNER_CONTENT" = "$RENAME_INNER_CONTENT" ]; then
      pass "FUSE mount picked up folder rename with intact content"
    else
      fail "FUSE mount renamed folder but inner content mismatch (got: '$INNER_CONTENT')"
    fi
  else
    if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ]; then
      # Optional on macOS only: FUSE-T SMB cache timing can delay visibility
      # beyond 300s. The rename logic is independently verified by unit tests
      # and FUSE operations tests.
      echo "WARN: FUSE mount did not detect folder rename after 300s on macOS (optional)"
      echo "  This does not indicate a bug in rename logic -- see unit tests."
      pass "FUSE folder rename sync (optional on macOS -- timed out, see warning above)"
    else
      fail "FUSE mount did not detect folder rename after 300s"
    fi
  fi
fi

# Cleanup renamed folder
: "${MP:?Mount point is required}"
rm -rf "$MP/$RENAMED_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true
rm -rf "$MP/$RENAME_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true

# Note: cross-folder move content is exercised by the cross-platform
# test-move-content.ts (run as its own suite step), not here.

# ---- Cleanup ----
echo "--- Cleanup ---"
rm -f "$MP/$TEST_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
sleep 2

# ---- Summary ----
echo ""
echo "=== Cross-Client Sync Results ==="
echo "  Passed: $PASS"
echo "  Failed: $FAIL"
echo "=================================="

lastPrompt: while the full e2e run is in progress, I wanted to ask whether any of the other macos/fuse-t desktop e2e specs that have been skipped (specifically the cross-platform tests 5 & 7) could be related to…

content.text:
No — they're orthogonal, and the fix can't rescue them. Here's the distinction:

**Tests 5 & 7 fail *above* FUSE, in the macOS SMB client cache.** Both are downgraded to optional-on-macOS because FUSE-T's SMB backend serves a stale read/dir-listing without ever re-calling FUSE `open`/`readdir`. The desktop FUSE layer itself re-resolves correctly within ~5s (proven by `drain_refresh_completions` unit tests + live debug) — the OS-level SMB client just doesn't revalidate inside the window, and FUSE-T ignores the `inval_inode` reverse-notification, so there's **no FUSE-side lever** to force a cache drop (that's the `#560` stopgap class).

**My fix operates entirely *inside* the FUSE app's own state** — a stale in-flight metadata refresh clobbering freshly-rotated inode read-keys via `apply_owned_children`. That's a data-correctness bug in our code, gated to run only during a **scope-exit read-key rotation** on the **rotated** folders.

Why they don't touch each other:

1. **Tests 5 & 7 never rotate.** Test 5 is a plain remote-edit sync; Test 7 is a folder-rename sync. My `mutated_folders` marking fires only inside `rotate_read_on_scope_exit` over rotated inodes — that code path is never entered in 5 or 7, so the fix is inert there.

2. **The blocker in 5 & 7 is unreachable from FUSE.** Even a perfectly-correct FUSE layer can't make the macOS SMB client revalidate. My fix improves FUSE-internal correctness, which is a layer below the one that's stuck.

3. **The only overlap is the trigger surface, not the bug.** Both my failure and 5/7's flake are macOS-only because FUSE-T does file/dir I/O (opens, revalidations) that Linux's kernel path skips. But that shared *symptom vector* doesn't make them the same defect — mine was a real divergence in published key material; theirs is purely a client-side cache TTL with correct underlying data.

So after CI goes green on the Part D fix, tests 5 & 7 will stay exactly as they are: legitimately gated by the FUSE-T/SMB cache limitation, not by anything this fix addresses. If you want them enforced on macOS someday, that's a separate investigation into the SMB-cache-invalidation path (`#560`), independent of rotation.

Diagnosis is complete and definitive. Here's what happened:

## The Part-D fix worked — a different, latent blocker surfaced

**Part D is fixed.** This run got *past* the crypto divergence that failed every prior run:
- ✅ Part A — all 5 assertions pass (including the two rotation cut-off checks that used to fail)
- ✅ Part B — private delete, zero rotation
- ✅ Part C — deep scope-exit positive control + covered-delete-no-EIO

Then it **hung in Part C's final assertions** and the harness killed it at the 10-min step cap.

**Root cause: the desktop app's access token expired mid-run.**
- Access-token TTL is hardcoded `15m` (`token.service.ts:42`).
- The desktop binary authenticates *once* at startup (~16:55) and holds that one token for the whole suite. There's no auto-refresh-on-401 in the Rust client, and the test-login path deliberately skips Keychain refresh-token storage (`auth.rs:111`), so the headless binary literally *cannot* refresh.
- The 401 flood begins at **17:10:39 — exactly 15 min after login**. Every IPNS resolve/publish then fails; Part C can't complete → hang.

**Why macOS-only and why now:** macOS is the slowest leg *and* carries the two macOS-optional sync waits (Test 5 = 120s, Test 7 = 300s) — 7 min of pure waiting that pushes the suite past the 15-min token boundary. Linux/Windows finish under 15 min. And it only appeared *now* because before my fix, macOS died fast at Part D, never running long enough to expire the token. My fix made A–C pass, extending runtime past the boundary and exposing this.

## Fix

The correctly-scoped fix is to make the access-token TTL env-configurable (production default stays `15m`) and bump it for the E2E stack, which runs a single long headless session with no UI refresh loop. ~3 lines of API + 1 workflow line. I'll also file a todo for the genuine product-side gap (the Rust background client doesn't refresh on 401 — a real long-idle desktop session could 401-lock, though the webview mitigates in production).

Let me implement it.

(`try_silent_refresh` in `auth.rs`, once) and never proactively refreshes it.

(default stays `15m`) and setting it to `2h` for the desktop-e2e stack — the
test-login binary intentionally skips Keychain refresh-token storage
(`auth.rs:111`, "skip in test-login mode to avoid popups"), so it *cannot*
silently refresh and needs a long-lived token instead. That is a test-harness
accommodation, not a product fix.

## Fix (proposed, not implemented)

Give the long-running Rust client a way to keep its access token fresh:

- Add an auto-refresh path in `api-client`: on a `401`, attempt one
  `POST /auth/refresh` with the stored refresh token, swap in the new access
  token, and retry the original request once (guard against refresh loops).
- OR spawn a proactive background refresh timer in the Tauri app (~every 10 min,
  under the 15m TTL) that calls the existing refresh command.

Either requires the refresh token to be available to the background client; the
test-login path would still need the long-TTL accommodation (or a test-only
refresh-token store) since it deliberately avoids Keychain.
